This project serves as the capstone assignment for the Fundamentals of C Programming course. The objective is to design and implement a complete software application by integrating concepts such as modular programming, file handling, dynamic memory allocation, recursion, pointers, and user-defined data structures. Emphasis is placed on writing efficient, well-documented, and maintainable C code while following good programming practices.

📄 Project Statement 📑 Final Report 💻 Source Code 📊 Presentation Slides 📊 Introduction to Statistics and Computation of Data Statistical Analysis of Real-World Data Project Description
The project involves analysing a real-world dataset using fundamental statistical techniques. The objective is to perform data cleaning, exploratory data analysis, estimation, hypothesis testing, and graphical visualisation using statistical software, followed by interpreting the results in a clear and reproducible manner.
Submittables
📄 Project Statement 📑 Final Report 💻 R Source Files 📈 R Markdown Notebook 📊 Presentation Slides ⚙️ Design and Analysis of Algorithms (DAA) Travelling Salesman Problem Project Description
The project investigates the Travelling Salesman Problem (TSP), one of the classical NP-hard optimisation problems. It focuses on implementing and comparing exact and approximation algorithms, analysing their computational complexity, and experimentally evaluating their performance on benchmark instances. Particular emphasis is placed on algorithm design, correctness, efficiency, and empirical analysis.

This project focuses on the implementation and analysis of fundamental data structures and algorithms. The objective is to design efficient implementations, evaluate their asymptotic performance, and experimentally compare their practical behaviour under different workloads. The project reinforces algorithmic thinking together with good software engineering practices.

Well I guess this marks the end of my bachelor’s truly, so this moment, the moment when I am having a cake while solo travelling in a train, is special, this moment deserves to be written about.
Most people would say their bachelor’s ended on 5th May 2026 (I’m not that good with dates), or probably end of May, when our results were announced. To me, who had his ideas developed from pop-culture, Bachelor’s was the best period of someone’s life and initially, I thought I couldn’t be more wrong about it. Going into ISI Bangalore (so called tier A), I was amazed to see - nothing. No proper infrastructure, no courts, no swimming pool, no rules, and overall, is still the smallest university camous I’ve been till date.
Journey # Initial resitance to Bhopal - IIT k messup - Sammy SN Bhatt offer - aritrabha and me planning - parents persuassion - the hot weather - the packing - missing my laptop charger and headphone - from RAC to CNF side lower - solo trip - morisaki bookshop - station approach meet iiserb student - auto share and night ride to campus - aritrabha meetup - dinner and late night walk (the amazement)
The bad phase (and a rushed decision) # Meeting prof with 1st proj - meeting co-intern - scheduling other meets - visits to the library - watching movie “Dead Poet’s Society” - loss of charger - the mood shift - IISC selection - the insta post - the depressed talks with Sammy - all time with Aritra - Shruti’s despair - taking too many projects - booking off tickets - worried about future.
The Good Phase # Meantime meal shift - from only Aritrabha to Aritra - met with some people, kUheli and Ayushi - sometimes have dinner with them - internal jokes - nescafe maggie - the contrast with IIT G - realised as we talked more with other people - the card group - the volleyball invitation - the awkwardness slowly goes away - nightime badminton and convo - other people of the group, sattu and Swati, and NIT Kuru (funny cause Har Katha Sangram ki is playing in bg) suicides dinner - charger delivered - and the plan started for Aritra’s b’day
The Better Phase # The changing point was probably the B’day plan - invitation to K and T and D (called Y) - extended to everyone - included even Shampoo in the plan - the order delivery dynamics - the group created - the surprise played out - the swiftie meetup - the UNO game and starting of a group. The next day - UNO meetup - The Rasgulla gift - the free treat - Entry of R - could see them in a reading group - FOMO - next lunch suggest Van vihar trip - random entry - joining the group - goes on to be better from now. After dinner plans to badminton - Random plans to SAnchi, Obsession, Ujjain - the spending bound over - Intro of M - meeting of other new people llike DHaram, Harshit - introduction of Mafia, Poker, COdenames - eagerly waiting everyday to complete dinner - even at dinner at wonderful convos with everyone - the talktime with family and Sammy went better - could see improvement in projects - teaching and learning new things everyday - sounding repetative probably but its true - the midsommer and discussion - had the best time in any internship ever (Should cover Ujjain specially - the planning - the aethism - general train journey - the tour - the return - sleeping) (Should alsocover a special section on the physics department - the ansh story in the start - his crush and weirdness to S - we started ignoring him - eventually understood. Specimen 2 - the weird intro - the school senior - the initial hate by Ayushi and everyone - the obsession with Aritra - seeing him everywhere even after ignoring - the long discussion about his cons while walk to hill - the big reveal of breakup - hate x100 - nanorods incident - intra department fight - reluctance at the name)
The Best Phase (Or probably worst?!) # It all started when there was 1 week remaining of my departure date - I knew I loved this group of people - bu that was the first time I realised what I meant to the group. Everyone was sad - and no one wanted to show it directly - I heard soo many compliments of me I started doubting their legitimacy - but then I saw their behavior - which was devoting their max time to me - the Mandir walk - the codenames - the politics discussion - the random Valorant plan - the trip to tekri - the stories - the last night game plan but disagreement - the final poker - the room convo or judging till late night - I got to know how much they cared - final closing bonds - the see off - the second reel - the hardest bye.

Summary # Yeah so let’s start from the begining # Backstory # All this started with a sigh. A sigh! of despair, when I realised that not only was Ed Sheeran coming to Bangalore when I would be available there, but also all the tickets of the show are booked till the price range of 10k. The sigh was an expression that makes me think that I can’t fulfill a wish I never knew I had, to attend a concert. Because that’s what people college, people of my age normally do right? Why should I be denied of the opportunity?
PS: I got to know later, which did not calm me down, that the shows of 8th November (the date of concert) was booked within 3 mins of the time when the ticket window opened. How jobless are these people, I can’t honestly sit infront of the computer (firstly I have to be updates with the arrival of Ed) always!
Ticket Booking # So the opportunity came to me quite unexpedtedly, actually during a bus ride from Kolkata to Durgapur. I did went with my mother for a reason, otherwise she would be asleep by that time and I would be hesitant to call and ask for the matter. As I said, I was dissapointed previously. So was my friend group. It so happens that we get to meet an individual during our visit, who was playing Ed songs in his guitar! Needless to say, this required a rant to my mother regarding my failure to attend a live concert if this talented individual followed by me opening the bookmyshow website as a habit to prove my point and wait! There is a new show available. Apparently seeing the demand of Ed in Bengalore (result of being housefull in 3 mins) they decided to perform for one more day, on 9th.
So what do you think? I took permission from my mother and put the poll in the group. Quite strangely, only Adrija accepted to go with me (her excitement made up for the absence of other people tbh). (Did I get a hint that it’s not expected of me by my parents of what I’m doing? Probably, but I thought it’s new to all of us so let’s try.) We got our tickets for 10k total, and we were relatively happy.
Band-width # After reading the BookMyShow guidelines for the 10th time, I was actually worried when the Bands required for us to gain entry into the concert didn’t arrive till 1st February. But obviously, it came, probably in one of the happiest moments of the day. I was having cheese Maggie, and got an invitation for another noodles treat, when I received the notification “your delivery is at your location”. I went hurriedly, and collected a rather flat packet (I didn’t know what to expect) which I assumed was carrying just the two bands (No idea how they look).

About # Who are we even? Welcome to my little corner of the internet. I’m Daibik Barik, a third-year undergrad at the Indian Statistical Institute, Bangalore Centre — a place where math gets serious and the coffee even more so.
This blog is a space for me to explore and share that curiosity — whether through math, stories, projects, or just things I find cool and worth writing about. I’m hoping it becomes a space where ideas can bounce around, grow, and maybe even surprise me once in a while.
Who am I? # I’m Daibik — a second-year undergrad who just really enjoys figuring things out. I’ve always been curious about how things work beneath the surface, especially when it comes to math. Patterns, probabilities, structures — I don’t always get them right away, but there’s something satisfying about slowly making sense of a tricky idea. I’m drawn to problems that make you pause, whether it’s a strange twist in graph theory or an unexpected result in probability.
At ISI, you’ll usually find me somewhere between the classroom, the mess, and late-night walks with friends that somehow turn into philosophical (or graph-theoretic) debates. I’m always looking to connect the abstract with the real, and I have this habit of seeing metaphors everywhere — maybe too often, but hey, it keeps things interesting.
Academics # Right now, I’m in my second year of the B.Math program at ISI Bangalore.
My current academic interests lie in combinatorics, graph theory, and probability, though I often stray into real analysis, discrete math, and whatever feels intellectually itchy at the moment.
I try to get involved in research-style projects whenever I can — not because I have everything figured out (I definitely don’t), but because I enjoy the process of sitting with an unfamiliar idea and trying to untangle it bit by bit. Sometimes it leads somewhere interesting, sometimes it doesn’t — but even then, I usually walk away with better questions, and that feels like a win.
What about other subjects?
Though math is my home turf, I’ve dipped my toes into computer science, physics, linguistics, and even storytelling. I like connecting dots between disciplines — that’s where some of the most beautiful ideas hide. Outside the Curriculum # Turns out, college isn’t just about problem sets and deadlines — I’ve also been part of a few clubs and events that bring a bit of unpredictability (and fun) to the mix.
With the Chess Club, I’ve helped organize various tournaments — including a multi-format intra-college series and a Variants Tour featuring some truly weird and fun chess versions. We also conducted “CHECKMATE,” the open chess tournament during our annual cultural fest, CHAOS. Planning it all was as strategic as playing it.
In the Cultural Committee, I helped put together events like Holi, Diwali, and Saraswati Puja — the kind of stuff that makes campus feel festive and a little less academic for a while. We also ran a campus-wide Treasure Hunt, hosted gaming evenings, handled merch distribution across over 100 students, and helped plan big moments like Freshers and Farewell. I was also part of the team behind CHAOS, our annual fest.
With the Movie Committee, I helped run weekly screenings of movies and matches in the college auditorium. We’d set up polls, take suggestions, and try to keep things fun and crowd-friendly.
Back in school at DAV Model, I was the Discipline Captain (Boys) — helping keep things running on time, handling weekly check-ins, and managing the rhythm of everyday school life. I also helped lead charity drives that collected items from over 6000 students and raised funds for orphanages and old age homes. Add to that co-organizing Teachers’ Day, Annual Day, Award Night — yeah, school kept me busy too.
Why Start a Blog? # I’ve been meaning to start something like this for a while — a space to write, reflect, and collect ideas that would otherwise just stay in my notes app or a fading notebook margin.
It’s partly for fun, partly for memory, and partly because I think putting thoughts into words sharpens them. I also want to connect with others — whether you’re into math, ideas, stories, or just here by accident. (Welcome either way.)
Adios # That’s all for now. If you made it this far — thank you!
I hope this blog grows into something thoughtful and messy and honest, like most good things are.
Let’s see what comes next :).
